'''Kimberly Flagg Sellers''' is an American statistician.
She has been the head of the statistics department at [[North Carolina State University]] since 2023, where she is the first Black woman in the university's history to lead a science department.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://sciences.ncsu.edu/news/kimberly-sellers-named-head-of-department-of-statistics/ | title=Kimberly Sellers Named Head of Department of Statistics | date=5 June 2023 }}</ref>  Previously, Dr. Sellers was a full professor of statistics at [[Georgetown University]] and {{r|gtfac}} a principal researcher in the Center for Statistical Research and Methodology of the [[United States Census Bureau]],{{r|amstat}}
the former chair of the Committee on Women in Statistics of the [[American Statistical Association]],{{r|amstat|mgb}} a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}}
She specializes in [[count data]] and [[statistical dispersion]], and is "the leading expert" on the [[Conway–Maxwell–Poisson distribution]] for count data.{{r|amstat|mgb}} She has also worked in the medical applications of statistics, and in [[image analysis]] for [[proteomics]].{{r|sees}}

==Education==
Sellers is [[African-American]], and was born in [[Washington, DC]].{{r|mgb|bwm}} Both her parents had advanced degrees;{{r|sees}} her father, pianist Thomas Flagg, became dean of fine arts at [[Howard University]].{{r|inspires}}
She set herself the goal of getting a doctorate in the mathematical sciences by the time she was in elementary school,{{r|mgb}}
and would read ''Black Issues in Higher Education'' with her father and look up the number of African-Americans to receive the Ph.D. in the mathematical sciences.{{r|sees}}

She was a Benjamin Banneker scholar at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]],{{r|bwm}} with [[Raymond L. Johnson]] as a mentor,{{r|mgb|bwm}} and earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics at Maryland in 1994 and 1998, respectively.{{r|amstat|cv}}
As a master's student at Maryland, she became interested in statistics after taking a class on the subject from Piotr Mikulski.{{r|mgb|inspires}}
Her master's thesis was ''Iterative methods for computing mean first passage times of Markov chains''.{{r|diss}}

She completed her Ph.D. in statistics at [[George Washington University]] in 2001, supported by the [[Gates Millennium Scholars Program]] as one of their first cohort of students.{{r|amstat}}
Her dissertation was ''Vague coherent systems'', with Nozer D. Singpurwalla as her [[doctoral advisor]].{{r|bwm|diss|mgp}}

==Career==
From 2001 to 2004, Sellers held a visiting assistant professorship and [[National Science Foundation]] supported postdoctoral scholarship at [[Carnegie Mellon University]], where she worked with [[Bill Eddy]] and [[Stephen Fienberg]].{{r|bwm}} In 2004, she became an assistant professor of [[biostatistics]] and [[epidemiology]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].{{r|cv}} She moved to Georgetown in 2006, at a time when the university was beginning a program in statistics,{{r|bwm}} and took a second affiliation with the Census Bureau in 2015.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Sellers became an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2018.{{r|isi}} She was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2021.{{r|fasa}}
